# Inputs and expression outputs

## Prepare aligned count matrices

| Object | Orientation | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `bulk` | Genes × individuals | Nonnegative integer RNA-sequencing counts |
| `reference` | Genes × reference cells | Raw single-cell or single-nucleus counts |
| `cell_type` | One label per reference column | Reference cell-type annotation |
| `reference_donor` | One donor ID per reference column | Biological origin of each reference cell |

Use unique, nonempty row and column names. Match gene identifiers, gene order and annotation order explicitly. Decide the modeled gene panel before fitting; retain that panel when preparing scorer features. Normalized expression and log-transformed counts are not substitutes for raw count inputs.

```r
stopifnot(identical(rownames(bulk), rownames(reference)))
stopifnot(length(cell_type) == ncol(reference),
          length(reference_donor) == ncol(reference),
          !anyDuplicated(rownames(bulk)),
          !anyDuplicated(colnames(bulk)),
          all(is.finite(bulk)), all(bulk >= 0),
          all(bulk == round(bulk)),
          all(is.finite(reference)), all(reference >= 0),
          all(reference == round(reference)))
```

## Run inference

```r
fit <- CDSeq2::cdseq2(
  bulk_data = bulk,
  reference_scRNA_count = reference,
  reference_scRNA_annotation = cell_type,
  reference_scRNA_donor = reference_donor,
  reference_aggregation = "pooled_counts",
  mcmc_iterations = 700,
  save_last_n_mc = 100,
  reference_precision = 1e6,
  n_chains = 1L, seed = 123L, cpu_number = 1,
  return_mcmc_arrays = FALSE,
  return_assignments = FALSE
)
```

These are example analysis settings, not universally optimal values. The paper's exact settings are in the frozen experiment scripts. Inspect convergence, reference similarity and the low-information diagnostics for your data. Multiple chains and longer runs may be appropriate.

## Understand the outputs

`fit$cdseq_result` contains one result per bulk sample. The two expression representations answer related but distinct questions:

| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `estGEP_RB` | Rao–Blackwellized posterior mean expression parameters; recommended by the package for general expression output |
| `estGEP_count` | Posterior mean reads allocated to each gene and cell type; used by the paper's benchmark and scorer training |
| `estProp_RB` | Rao–Blackwellized RNA-fraction estimates |
| `estProp` | Legacy RNA-fraction estimates used by the frozen paper workflow |
| `information` | Information and support diagnostics for interpreting the inferred profiles |

Use the same estimator, normalization and inference settings as the training benchmark when applying a scorer. A change in estimator can change the target being predicted.

The [tutorial extraction code](quickstart.qmd) creates `estimated_counts` on genes × types × samples and `rna_fractions` on samples × types. It verifies that allocated reads sum back to bulk counts and fractions sum to one. Preserve identifiers on every axis.

For the paper-compatible within-type expression scale:

```r
component_totals <- apply(estimated_counts, c(2, 3), sum)
stopifnot(all(component_totals > 0))
cpm <- sweep(estimated_counts, c(2, 3), component_totals, "/") * 1e6
log_expression <- log2(cpm + 0.5)
```

An RNA fraction is a share of the RNA represented in the modeled mixture. It is not automatically the proportion of cells: cell types can differ in RNA content. Likewise, within-type CPM describes relative expression on the modeled panel; it does not recover absolute transcript counts per cell.
